data.name: Advik
data.gender_notes: Advik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Advik is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘advai’ meaning ‘two’ and ‘k’ meaning ‘path’. In Hindu mythology, Advik is a name of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing the two paths of righteousness and sin that every soul must choose in life. The name Advik carries the meaning “Two paths” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Advik usually hope their child will grow to embody two paths and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Advik belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Two paths.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Advik total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Advik is an uncommon Hindu name, but it carries a rich cultural heritage as it is derived from Sanskrit language. In Hinduism, the number ‘two’ holds significant importance due to the duality of the universe - the duality of light and dark, male and female, good and evil, etc. The name Advik continues this theme of duality, implying the existence of both good and bad paths in life. It is also a name associated with Lord Vishnu, one of the primary deities in Hinduism, demonstrating the deep roots of this name in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Advik holds deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘advai,’ which means ‘non-dual,’ and ‘k’ which stands for ‘path.’ The name Advik symbolizes the concept of choosing between the path of righteousness and sin. In Hindu mythology, every soul must undertake a journey through life and make a choice between these two paths, often depicted as diverse yet interconnected rivers flowing beside each other. By carrying this name, an individual is constantly reminded of their duty to choose the path of righteousness and strive towards attaining spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Advik: The One with Unwavering Devotion. Symbolizing absolute dedication and devotion to the divine, Advik embodies the unyielding spirit of a devotee whose heart and mind are entirely consumed by the pursuit of the divine.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'advik', meaning 'absence of two'. This name is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and is believed to bring good fortune and prosperity to the bearer.

historical_references.reference: Advik was a king in ancient India, ruling over the Vatsa kingdom in the Magadha region during the 5th century BCE. He is best known for his patronage of Buddhism and for sheltering Buddha during a particular rainy season.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Vatsa kingdom, Magadha region, patronage of Buddhism

historical_references.reference: Advik is also mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, where he is described as a powerful and just king of the Bhoja dynasty in central India during the late 4th century BCE. He is revered for his wisdom and for his role in the Kurukshetra war.
historical_references.context: Hindu epic Mahabharata, Bhoja dynasty, central India, patron of wisdom, Kurukshetra war
